facts.text: Sprague was founded in 1888 when the Missouri Pacific Railroad reached the site, and it was named after Civil War veteran William Sprague and his wife Amy.
In 1912 and again in 1927, fires devastated much of Sprague's business district, reshaping the town's commercial core.
The 1963 Bluestem Conservation Dam created a 325‑acre lake, and surrounding land was turned into a 742‑acre recreational area.
Sprague prides itself on preserving historical, cultural, and natural heritage, encouraging guided growth and a wholesome lifestyle for residents.
The village maintains a deep commitment to environmental preservation while fostering progressive local business initiatives, reflecting its community values.
